ratings.comment: Anthro 104 is such an easy but interesting class. Lectures are not mandatory and few students attend. She speaks quite quickly and does not share slides, but lectures tended to be more application of the material, so I did not need to take notes during lecture. There are 3 open, non-proctored exams and 3 projects that were all easy.

I think that Dr. Schulte is a great professor, however the class itself requires a lot of reading. It takes a lot of time to complete the chapter readings each week, but doing so will set you up very well for lecture discussions.

This class was very easy, and professor was very passionate about what she was teaching. Lectures were not necessary to attend, but you should/have to go to discussion, which most of the time can be pretty engaging and entertaining. There are 3 online tests and 3 projects, but other than that, there's really nothing to worry about.

This class was really easy and Prof Schulte was very passionate in her lectures! She did talk fairly fast, making it hard to take notes and didn't share her slides, but reading the textbook will help fill in the gaps. Projects are solo and were really easy/borderline busywork. Your TA will be the biggest influence on your experience, though.

I like her a lot!! Sometimes rushes through lecture slides quite fast, and doesn't post the slides. It can be easy to lose attention for a second, and miss what she said on a previous slide. But, if you do the readings youll be fine!! Grading really depends on your TA, but for me grading has been pretty generous.

Didn't often go to lectures (oops) exams are all online + not proctored. Professor is interesting and engaging but just not my thing as I'm not an anthro major. LOVED my TA she was so so knowledgable and such a good teacher so I actually enjoyed going to discussion where attendance is mandatory. Mostly just busy work not super challenging.

I genuinely looked forward to this class every day we met. Discussions were lively and engaging. Papers were graded a bit more harshly than I think most of anthro professors I've had; however, I never felt like the grading was unfair.
